apps.summary: yt-dlp is a native open-source command-line downloader for publicly accessible web media and streams. Users are solely responsible for complying with applicable website Terms of Service and copyright laws.

apps.name: Anaconda / Miniconda
apps.summary: Anaconda and Miniconda provide official native Linux installers for Python and data-science environments.

apps.name: Snapmaker Luban
apps.summary: Snapmaker Luban provides official native Linux packages (.deb and AppImage) for 3D printing, laser engraving, and CNC workflows on Snapmaker machines.

apps.name: Antigravity
apps.summary: Antigravity provides official native Linux packages from its download page.

apps.name: Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)
apps.summary: Windows Subsystem for Linux runs a Linux environment inside Windows — when switching directly to Linux, you are already running native Linux and no replacement package is needed.

apps.name: Outlook for Windows

alternatives.name: Mozilla Thunderbird
alternatives.tagline: Open-source native Linux email, calendar, and contacts client

alternatives.name: Outlook on the Web
alternatives.tagline: Official Outlook web interface in any Linux browser

alternatives.name: Betterbird
alternatives.tagline: Community-maintained fork of Thunderbird with extra refinements

apps.summary: Outlook for Windows does not provide a native Linux desktop client. Outlook on the Web runs directly in Linux browsers, and Mozilla Thunderbird or Betterbird provide native desktop email and calendar support.

apps.name: Microsoft Clipchamp

alternatives.name: Kdenlive
alternatives.tagline: Open-source multi-track native Linux video editor with hardware acceleration

alternatives.name: Clipchamp Web
alternatives.tagline: Browser-based Clipchamp editor in Chromium-based Linux browsers

alternatives.name: Shotcut
alternatives.tagline: Clean, approachable cross-platform open-source video editor

apps.summary: Microsoft Clipchamp's desktop app is Windows-focused, while Clipchamp Web runs in supported Chromium-based browsers on Linux. For native offline video editing, Kdenlive and Shotcut are widely used open-source Linux editors.

apps.name: Windhawk

alternatives.name: GNOME Tweaks
alternatives.tagline: Customize fonts, themes, window controls, and desktop behavior on GNOME

alternatives.name: KDE Plasma Built-in Customization
alternatives.tagline: KDE Plasma includes extensive native panel, widget, theme, and shortcut customization

apps.summary: Windhawk customizes Windows UI internals and is Windows-only. Linux desktop environments such as KDE Plasma and GNOME offer extensive native customization, themes, widgets, and extensions.

apps.name: Rockstar Games Launcher

alternatives.name: Lutris
alternatives.tagline: Independent open-source Linux gaming manager supporting Wine and Proton runners

alternatives.name: Steam (Proton)
alternatives.tagline: Runs Steam-purchased Rockstar titles via Steam Play / Proton

alternatives.name: Bottles
alternatives.tagline: Sandboxed Wine prefix manager for Windows game launchers

apps.summary: Rockstar Games Launcher does not provide an official native Linux client. Independent third-party compatibility tools such as Steam Proton, Lutris, or Bottles can run many single-player titles, though online multiplayer anti-cheat (such as BattlEye in GTA Online) may restrict Linux access per publisher policy. Users are responsible for complying with all applicable EULAs and Terms of Service.

apps.name: Xbox App (Windows)

alternatives.name: Xbox Cloud Gaming (Web)
alternatives.tagline: Stream eligible Xbox Game Pass Ultimate titles directly in a Linux browser

apps.summary: The Windows Xbox desktop app and local Microsoft Store / PC Game Pass game downloads are Windows-only. Eligible Xbox Cloud Gaming titles can be played in supported Linux browsers.

hardware_drivers.name: NVIDIA GPU & Drivers
hardware_drivers.summary: NVIDIA provides official native Linux GPU drivers (including open-kernel modules for RTX 20-series / Turing and newer). Most distributions (Ubuntu/Mint Driver Manager, Fedora RPM Fusion, Arch packages, Pop!_OS NVIDIA ISO) provide guided driver installation without manual .run installers.

hardware_drivers.name: Intel Graphics, Wireless & Platform
hardware_drivers.summary: Intel integrated and Arc GPUs (i915/xe + Mesa), Wi-Fi (iwlwifi), Bluetooth, and chipset drivers are built directly into the Linux kernel and update automatically with your system. Intel oneAPI Level Zero compute runtimes are also available natively on Linux.

hardware_drivers.name: AMD Radeon GPU & Chipset
hardware_drivers.summary: AMD Radeon GPU drivers (amdgpu + Mesa/RADV) and Ryzen chipset drivers are built directly into the Linux kernel and update with your distribution. Optional open-source tools such as LACT or CoreCtrl provide graphical fan and power controls.

hardware_drivers.name: Qualcomm Snapdragon / ARM64 Platform
hardware_drivers.summary: Windows-on-ARM (Snapdragon X / ARM64) PCs require an ARM64 (aarch64) Linux distribution with a recent kernel (Linux 6.11+) and device-tree/firmware support for your specific laptop model. Always test Wi-Fi, audio, sleep, and display on an ARM64 Live USB first, and note that x86-64 software/games require ARM64 builds or translation layers.

hardware_drivers.name: MediaTek Wi-Fi & Bluetooth
hardware_drivers.summary: Modern MediaTek Wi-Fi 6/6E/7 and Bluetooth adapters (mt7921e / mt7925e) are supported natively in recent Linux kernels and linux-firmware packages.

hardware_drivers.name: Qualcomm Atheros / Killer Wi-Fi & Ethernet
hardware_drivers.summary: Qualcomm Atheros and Killer Wi-Fi/Ethernet adapters (ath10k / ath11k / ath12k) are supported directly in modern Linux kernels and linux-firmware; Windows companion control panels are not required on Linux.

hardware_drivers.name: Broadcom Wi-Fi & Bluetooth
hardware_drivers.summary: Many Broadcom Ethernet adapters work natively in Linux, while some Broadcom Wi-Fi chipsets require enabling non-free firmware or the distribution's broadcom-wl driver package. Test Wi-Fi on a Linux Live USB or have Ethernet/USB tethering available during initial setup.

hardware_drivers.name: Realtek Audio & Network
hardware_drivers.summary: Realtek audio (ALSA/PipeWire) and Ethernet/Wi-Fi drivers are built into the Linux kernel. Use desktop sound settings or open-source EasyEffects for equalizer and audio routing.

hardware_drivers.name: Lenovo Vantage / ThinkPad / Legion Utilities
hardware_drivers.summary: Lenovo ThinkPad, IdeaPad, and Legion hardware controls (hotkeys, battery charge thresholds, thermal profiles) are widely supported in the Linux kernel (thinkpad_acpi / ideapad_laptop) and firmware updates are delivered natively via LVFS / fwupd.

hardware_drivers.name: Dell / Alienware Support & Firmware Utilities
hardware_drivers.summary: Dell systems have broad Linux kernel support and publish BIOS/UEFI firmware updates through the open Linux Vendor Firmware Service (fwupd). Windows companion apps like SupportAssist and Dell Optimizer are not needed on Linux.

hardware_drivers.name: HP / OMEN Companion & Printer Utilities
hardware_drivers.summary: HP laptops work with standard Linux kernel ACPI drivers and fwupd firmware updates on supported models. HP printers and scanners are supported natively on Linux via CUPS driverless printing and HP's open-source HPLIP package.

hardware_drivers.name: Microsoft Surface Drivers & App
hardware_drivers.summary: Basic features on Microsoft Surface devices work in standard Linux kernels, while full touch, pen, battery, and camera support on many Surface models is provided by the independent open-source linux-surface kernel project (check their device support matrix).

hardware_drivers.name: MSI Center / Dragon Center Utilities
hardware_drivers.summary: MSI motherboard and laptop hardware works via Linux kernel drivers (msi-ec / msi-wmi). For RGB lighting and fan controls on supported hardware, check open-source OpenRGB and MControlCenter.

hardware_drivers.name: Acer NitroSense / PredatorSense / Care Center
hardware_drivers.summary: Standard Acer laptop controls work via the Linux kernel acer-wmi module; Windows companion dashboards such as NitroSense and PredatorSense are Windows-only.

hardware_drivers.name: Gigabyte / AORUS Control Center
hardware_drivers.summary: Gigabyte motherboards and GPUs work natively with Linux kernel drivers; Windows-only companion suites can be replaced with open-source OpenRGB and lm-sensors/CoolerControl on supported models.

hardware_drivers.name: Apple Boot Camp & Hardware Support
hardware_drivers.summary: Intel Macs with Apple T2 security chips can run Linux via the community t2linux kernel/project; older Intel Macs work directly with mainline Linux kernels.

hardware_drivers.name: Printers & Scanners (Canon / Epson / Brother / Xerox)
hardware_drivers.summary: Most modern network and USB printers work automatically on Linux with zero driver installs via CUPS driverless printing (AirPrint / IPP Everywhere) and SANE for scanning; Brother, Canon, Epson, and HP also offer native Linux drivers for older models.

hardware_drivers.name: Drawing Tablets (Wacom / Huion / XP-Pen / Gaomon)
hardware_drivers.summary: Wacom and many Huion/XP-Pen drawing tablets are supported directly in the Linux kernel (wacom/DIGImend), and open-source OpenTabletDriver adds low-latency area and button configuration across hundreds of tablets.

hardware_drivers.name: SSD & Storage Utilities (Samsung / WD / Crucial / Kingston / Seagate)
hardware_drivers.summary: NVMe and SATA SSD health, TRIM, and SMART monitoring are built into Linux via GNOME Disks, smartmontools, nvme-cli, and fwupd (which delivers SSD firmware updates for supported drives).

hardware_drivers.name: Display Docks, Stream Decks & VR Companion Apps
hardware_drivers.summary: DisplayLink publishes an official Linux driver (evdi) for USB docks; monitors can adjust brightness/inputs via ddcutil; Elgato Stream Deck works with open-source StreamController/Boatswain; wireless PCVR headsets can connect on Linux via ALVR or WiVRn.

hardware_drivers.name: USB Audio Interfaces & Gaming Headsets
hardware_drivers.summary: Class-compliant USB microphones, audio interfaces (such as Focusrite Scarlett), and gaming headsets work natively on Linux via ALSA and PipeWire. Windows companion apps are Windows-only; use EasyEffects or alsa-scarlett-gui on Linux.

hardware_drivers.name: Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server
hardware_drivers.summary: Microsoft publishes official native Linux ODBC Driver packages (msodbcsql17/18) for Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora/RHEL, and openSUSE.

hardware_drivers.name: Npcap / WinPcap Packet Capture Driver
hardware_drivers.summary: Npcap is a Windows-only packet capture driver used by tools such as Nmap and Wireshark on Windows. Linux provides native kernel packet capture (libpcap / AF_PACKET) out of the box.

hardware_drivers.name: Controller & Virtual Input Drivers (ViGEm / HidHide / FakerInput)
hardware_drivers.summary: Linux includes native kernel drivers for PlayStation (DualSense/DualShock 4), Xbox, Nintendo Switch, and generic USB/Bluetooth controllers alongside Steam Input — Windows virtual bus drivers such as ViGEmBus, HidHide, and FakerInput are not needed on Linux.

hardware_drivers.name: Spatial Audio & OEM Sound Enhancements (Dolby / THX / DTS)
hardware_drivers.summary: Standard USB and analog audio output works natively on Linux via ALSA and PipeWire. Vendor spatial-audio companion apps (Dolby Access, THX Spatial Audio, DTS) are Windows-only; open-source EasyEffects provides system-wide equalizer and audio effects on Linux.

hardware_drivers.name: Logitech Peripherals & Software
hardware_drivers.summary: Logitech mice, keyboards, and receivers work out of the box on Linux via standard kernel HID drivers. Official Logitech configuration suites are Windows/macOS-only; independent open-source tools such as Solaar (supported receivers/devices), Piper (supported gaming mice), and Input Remapper provide Linux configuration.

hardware_drivers.name: Razer Peripherals & Software
hardware_drivers.summary: Razer keyboards, mice, and USB headsets work via Linux kernel HID and USB audio drivers. Razer Synapse is Windows-only; independent open-source projects such as OpenRazer + Polychromatic or OpenRGB support lighting and DPI controls on many models (check each project's hardware compatibility list).

hardware_drivers.name: Corsair Peripherals & RGB Software
hardware_drivers.summary: Corsair keyboards, mice, and headsets work via standard Linux kernel HID and audio drivers. Corsair iCUE is Windows/macOS-only; independent open-source tools such as ckb-next and OpenRGB support lighting and key controls on many Corsair devices (check hardware compatibility lists).

hardware_drivers.name: ASUS OEM Utilities (GlideX / Armoury Crate / MyASUS)
hardware_drivers.summary: ASUS Windows companion utilities are Windows-only. For phone and cross-device continuity similar to GlideX, consider open-source KDE Connect or LocalSend on Linux; for supported ASUS laptops, the community asusctl tool manages fan profiles and keyboard lighting.

hardware_drivers.name: Laptop OEM Control Center & Fn Hotkeys
hardware_drivers.summary: Standard laptop hotkeys (brightness, volume, Wi-Fi) work natively through the Linux kernel ACPI/WMI subsystem. For Clevo/Tongfang fan and keyboard controls, check open-source Tuxedo Control Center or distribution-specific laptop utilities.

hardware_drivers.name: Custom Keyboard & Peripheral Drivers
hardware_drivers.summary: Standard typing and pointing work natively on Linux via kernel USB HID drivers. Proprietary Windows key-remapping utilities are Windows-only; consider open-source Input Remapper on Linux.
